Corpulence

/KOR-pyuh-luhns/ - the stress falls on KOR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Corpulence means extreme fatness.

The novelist gave every one of his villains a comfortable corpulence, as if appetite itself were a clue.

Worked Example

Season after season, the opera company's costume shop let out the famous tenor's doublet another inch, until the wardrobe mistress observed that his corpulence was outpacing his reviews.

Corpulence is the precise choice because it names genuine, extreme fatness in a formal, almost clinical register. Plumpness would be too affectionate and heft too vague — corpulence says plainly that the body has grown very fat, while keeping a dignified tone.

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — plumpness → stoutness → corpulence

plumpness vs. corpulence

plumpness vs. corpulence: Plumpness is mild, even affectionate — a well-fed roundness that stops far short of corpulence.

stoutness vs. corpulence

stoutness vs. corpulence: Stoutness goes further than plumpness — a solid, settled heaviness — but still stops short of corpulence, which names outright extreme fatness.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — corp-

Root — corp-: body (Latin corpus)

Suffix — -ulence

Suffix — -ulence: fullness, abundance of

Put it together

Put it together: Corp- (body) + -ulence (fullness of) = fullness of body. Latin corpus, 'body,' anchors a whole English family — corpse, corps, corporation — and corpulence is what the body has when there is simply a great deal of it.

Use the root in a new word: incorporate

Use the root in a new word: incorporate: The city voted to incorporate the harbor district into its downtown plan.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / old-fashioned

Corpulence keeps its dignity: it states extreme fatness in a formal, faintly antique register, which is why historians and novelists favor it. For gentler everyday description, plumpness or stoutness is kinder; for a medical chart, obesity. Corpulence belongs to people and animals — bulk in objects or buildings is just bulk.
